empty.title: Your knowledge base
empty.body: Add your Obsidian vault folder to read it here, sync it between machines and give it to your assistants over MCP.

space.cloudWarningTitle: This space lives in a cloud-synced folder
space.cloudWarningBody: Synology Drive, iCloud or Dropbox rewrite files while git uses them, and git ends up corrupted. Move the space to a local folder and let SincroGitExclude sync it.
space.missingTitle: The folder of the space cannot be found

note.privateLink: Points to a private space: the people you share this space with will see a broken link.
note.frontmatterError: The frontmatter is not valid YAML: {{error}}

search.semanticOff: Turn on semantic search in Settings to search by meaning.
search.hint: ↑↓ to move, Enter to open, Esc to close

dialog.name: Name
dialog.cloudWarning: The folder is inside a cloud-synced folder. For git, use a local folder.
dialog.existingMeta: The folder already has a space identity: {{name}}.
dialog.insideSpace: It is inside the space “{{name}}”: it will be added as a nested space.
dialog.gitRemoteHint: HTTPS or SSH, without any token in the URL.
dialog.sftpPassphrase: Key passphrase (optional, stored in the system keychain)
dialog.trustHint: Compare it with the server (ssh-keyscan or the NAS console) before trusting it.
dialog.onWrite: Sync after every write (from the app, assistants or Obsidian)
dialog.autoCommit: Commit Obsidian edits to git even without syncing
dialog.agentWrite: Assistants can write in this space
dialog.reviewBeforePush: Review what assistants write before it leaves this computer
dialog.shared: Shared with other people (blocks secrets and turns on review)
dialog.removeConfirm: Forget “{{name}}”? Nothing is deleted from disk.
dialog.relocateBody: The space is copied to the new folder and the app switches to it. The old folder is left alone: stop syncing it with Drive once you checked the copy, and do not delete it inside the synced folder because the deletion would reach every machine.
dialog.relocateConfirm: Copy and use the new folder
dialog.encryptedRemote: This destination already holds an encrypted space

gitAuth.label: Authentication
gitAuth.system: The git setup of this computer
gitAuth.systemHint: Uses the SSH agent or the credentials saved in git (keychain, Git Credential Manager, gh, glab).
gitAuth.tokenHint: For private repositories over HTTPS in Gitea, Forgejo, GitLab, GitHub or others. The token is stored in the system keychain and only sent to this server.
gitAuth.ghHint: Asks gh for the token on every sync, with the account you choose even if it is not the active one. Stores nothing.
gitAuth.ssh-keyHint: For SSH remotes, with that key and without trying others. If it has a passphrase, load it in the agent first.
gitAuth.stored: Stored in the keychain. Type another one to change it.
gitAuth.onlyWindow: The token can only be typed in the app window.
gitAuth.createToken: Create the token on the server
gitAuth.unencrypted: That remote is not encrypted: the token will not be sent. Use https.
gitAuth.okEmpty: Connection works. The repository is empty.
gitAuth.public: Anyone can read this repository without signing in.
gitAuth.notPublic: It cannot be read without signing in. Users of a restricted server can still read its public repositories.

permissions.github: Fine-grained token of the repository with Contents: Read and write. The user can stay empty.
permissions.gitlab: Personal or project token with write_repository. The user can stay empty.
permissions.gitea: Token with write permission on repositories, and your user.
permissions.other: Your user and a token or app password with write permission.

sync.title: Sync
sync.noRemote: This space only lives on this computer. Choose a storage in its settings to sync it.
sync.openRepo: Open the repository in the browser
sync.logHint: Keeps the last 200 syncs that moved files or had problems. Syncs that found no changes are left out.

trigger.write: After a change in the app
trigger.assistant-write: After a change by the assistant
trigger.external: After a change outside the app

sync.tooBig: The change is too big to show here.

history.title: History of {{name}}
history.empty: No history: the space does not use git or the note is new.
history.pick: Pick a version to see what changed.

crypto.title: Encryption
crypto.off: Notes travel unencrypted to the remote storage.
crypto.on: What leaves this computer is end-to-end encrypted.
crypto.needsBackend: Choose where the space is stored first.
crypto.noKeychain: This system has no usable keychain: the passphrase will be asked on every start.
crypto.wizardIntro: The server will only see encrypted files: not the content, not the names, not the folders. The copy on this computer stays readable so Obsidian can open it.
crypto.wizardRemote: Use an empty destination: a new folder or repository. The history of a repository that already had plain notes would keep them.
crypto.wordsIntro: Write these 24 words on paper and keep them somewhere safe. The passphrase or this code recover the space. If you lose both and all your devices, nobody can recover the notes.
crypto.wordsConfirm: Type the requested words to check you have them:
crypto.removeConfirm: Access for “{{name}}” will be removed and the key of the space will change; everything is encrypted again on the next sync. What they already downloaded stays with them.
crypto.pendingHint: Check that the other device shows exactly these words before approving.
crypto.requestSent: Request sent. On a device that already has access, open this space and approve the request from “{{name}}”.
crypto.pairingBody: The device that approved the request showed some words. If they are these, confirm:
crypto.adoptHint: The destination already holds an encrypted space. Open it with its passphrase or request access from this computer.
crypto.newRecoveryBody: The previous code stops working. Write this one down:
crypto.ownerOnly: Only the owner can manage access: unlock with the passphrase.

repo.linked: This repository is linked to “{{note}}” in {{space}}.
repo.notLinked: This repository has no note in the knowledge base.
repo.unlinkConfirm: The files the app added to the repository and their exclude entries are removed. The note is left alone.
repo.forgetInVault: Also forget the link in the vault (other machines will stop suggesting it)
repo.createNote: Create the note from the template if it does not exist
repo.noteMissing: The note does not exist: it will be created
repo.integrations: What is added to the repository (all in .git/info/exclude, nothing in .gitignore)
repo.pointerHint: Readable pointer: space, note and MCP.
repo.mcpJsonHint: Project MCP server. The token comes from the SGE_KB_TOKEN variable.
repo.sessionHookHint: Loads the project note at the start of each session, even with the app closed.
repo.agentsMdHint: Managed block for Codex, Cursor and other agents.
repo.suggestion: The vault has a note for this repository: {{note}}. Link it on this computer?
repo.remoteMode: The knowledge base lives on another computer (remote MCP)
repo.worktreeNote: Works in worktrees too: the exclude file is shared.

settings.title: Knowledge base
settings.semanticHint: Search by meaning as well as by words. Embeddings are computed on this computer and never synced.
settings.localDownload: Downloaded once (~{{size}} MB) to the data folder.
settings.apiKeyEnv: Environment variable with the API key
settings.leavesDevice: The text of your notes is sent to that service to compute embeddings.
